checks: Least-active global maximality and degree-one homogeneity give a k-dimensional active span by the frozen independence predecessor. Even when positive homogeneity is stated only for positive scalars, it implies f_i(0)=2f_i(0), so f_i(0)=0 and the required identity extends to scalar zero.

The domain of the quotient map is an external direct sum and has dimension equal to the sum of the individual dimensions, even if the E_i intersect inside ambient coordinate space. Its codomain has dimension m−k.

If the dimension bound fails, rank-nullity supplies a nonzero tuple with sum in the active span. The compensation predecessor applies to this tuple because each selected row is strictly positive and C² there, and global maximality implies local maximality.

For each finite selected row, Taylor expansion of its own remainder is s_i² times its directional Hessian value divided by two plus o(s_i²). The scale factor times s_i² is t²/(1+t a_i), giving the exact leading t² coefficient and an o(t²) total error.

Every quadratic term is nonnegative and a nonzero component makes one strictly positive. The resulting increase contradicts the maximum for sufficiently small nonzero t. Purely scaled rows need no differentiability. Zero-dimensional selected subspaces and the empty set reduce consistently to the row-count bound.
